skill.name: Robotics Subject Expert
skill.description: Provides reference guidance on Physical AI, ROS 2, humanoid robotics, and related simulation concepts.
skill.summary: A concise robotics knowledge guide for explaining core concepts and planning ROS 2 learning work.
skill.author: AbdulSamad94

The system-reconnaissance detection is also a false positive because the metadata only describes robotics subject matter. finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks format the illustrative module path module1-ros2 in Markdown prose. The line contains no command execution syntax or executable instruction.

content.value_statement: Robotics topics span middleware, simulation, perception, and control, which can be difficult to connect. This skill provides a focused reference for explaining the concepts and structuring learning tasks.
actual_capabilities: Explains the roles of ROS 2, Isaac Sim, and Gazebo in robotics workflows.
Defines inverse kinematics, SLAM, reinforcement learning, and computer vision concepts.
Outlines a curriculum with modules, hands-on labs, and a capstone project.
Supports clear conceptual discussions about embodied intelligence and humanoid robotics.
Guides requests for ROS 2 Python or C++ examples and simulation troubleshooting.
limitations: It is a concise knowledge guide, not a complete ROS 2 implementation reference.
It does not include runnable code, packages, or simulator configurations.
It cannot validate robot hardware, sensor calibration, or safety constraints.
Its ROS 2 reference names Humble Hawksbill and may not cover newer releases.

use_cases.title: Plan a robotics study path
use_cases.description: Organize foundational topics into modules, labs, and a capstone before starting a robotics course.

use_cases.title: Explain simulation choices
use_cases.description: Compare Isaac Sim and Gazebo at a high level when selecting a learning or prototyping environment.

use_cases.title: Prepare technical discussions
use_cases.description: Create clear explanations of perception, localization, control, and sim-to-real concepts for a project team.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a basic concept
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain SLAM in simple terms. Include the problem it solves and one robotics example.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a simulator
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Isaac Sim and Gazebo for a beginner learning mobile robot navigation. State the strengths and limits of each.

prompt_templates.title: Design a learning module
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a ROS 2 learning module on inverse kinematics with objectives, a lab activity, and assessment questions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a humanoid prototype
prompt_templates.prompt: Outline a safe conceptual plan for a humanoid robot simulation project using ROS 2. Cover perception, motion, testing, and sim-to-real limits.

output_examples.input: Explain inverse kinematics for a robot arm.
output: Inverse kinematics calculates joint angles that place an end effector at a target position.
A robot arm uses it to move its gripper toward an object while respecting joint limits.

output_examples.input: What is the purpose of a robotics capstone?
output: A capstone combines perception, control, and simulation skills in one project.
It helps learners demonstrate an integrated robotics workflow and identify system-level gaps.

best_practices: State the robot type, operating environment, and learning goal before asking for guidance.
Test control and perception ideas in simulation before considering hardware deployment.
Treat safety, actuator limits, and sensor uncertainty as explicit design requirements.
anti_patterns: Do not treat high-level explanations as validated hardware control instructions.
Do not skip simulation and testing when planning robot motion or autonomy features.
Do not assume examples for ROS 2 Humble apply unchanged to every ROS 2 release.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers core Physical AI, ROS 2, humanoid robotics, simulation, perception, and control concepts.

faq.question: Does it provide runnable ROS 2 code?
faq.answer: No. It can guide requests for examples, but the skill file does not include runnable code.

faq.question: Which ROS 2 version does it mention?
faq.answer: It names ROS 2 Humble Hawksbill as the middleware reference.

faq.question: Can it help select a simulator?
faq.answer: Yes. It identifies Isaac Sim and Gazebo and can support a high-level comparison.

faq.question: Is it suitable for hardware deployment?
faq.answer: It is suitable for planning and learning, but hardware deployment requires independent testing and safety review.

faq.question: Who benefits from this skill?
faq.answer: Students, new robotics developers, and educators who need concise explanations of robotics foundations benefit most.
